title: Build own project and deployed it. Need a honest opinion. GEX Analysis platform with AutoScanner for signals
author: AlexxBrut_RU
selftext:
Hey everyone,

So I've finally finished building a project I've been grinding on for a while now, and I wanted to share it with you all.

It's a comprehensive stock analysis app that combines GEX (Gamma Exposure) analysis, AI-driven analysis based on Smart Money Concepts (SMC), GEX data, and automatically generated trendlines. Basically, I wanted a single tool that pulls together multiple analytical frameworks instead of juggling five different tabs.

For the AI side of things, I've been running everything through WorkbuddyAi using Deepseek V4 Flash + Kimi k3.  
The backend is built on FastAPI with SQLAlchemy and PostgreSQL. Celery handles async task processing, and Redis is used for caching data pulled from the fetchers. I also wrote a custom orchestration module from scratch that balances connections across fetchers so nothing gets rate-limited or banned. That part alone took a good chunk of time, but it works really smoothly now.  
Sign-up is handled through a Telegram bot.

**And yes, it's completely free right now**, mainly because I'm still actively testing and developing new features. I'd genuinely appreciate any feedback.

**What you can actually do with it:**

* **Triangle Scenario Analysis** — This one's pretty cool. You can model "what if" scenarios: if a company's revenue or earnings came in higher than expected, what would the stock price look like? How would the P/E ratio shift? It walks you through the math visually.
* **Smooth Candle Mode** — Instead of the usual choppy candle rendering, there's a special smooth regime that filters out noise and gives you a clearer picture of the actual price movement. Makes reading structure way easier.
* **Custom RSI Regime** — I built a modified RSI view that highlights specific points based on expected mathematical value rather than just the standard overbought/oversold zones. It surfaces levels you'd normally miss.
* **Quarterly Volatility Script** — I wrote a script that calculates stock volatility on a quarterly basis. It's great for spotting extreme at exact date that you might overlook on a longer chart.
* **AutoScanner -** The service has own AutoScanner which is based on my personal strategy which uses typical trend-following idea with some additionals. It helps to show that trend starts and it allows you to don't skip it.

Anyway, I'd love to hear what you guys think. If you try it out, drop your feedback — what works, what's confusing, what you'd want added. Still very much a work in progress, but I'm proud of where it's at.

Cheers! Thank you all in advance

My project here - [gexanalytic.tech](https://gexanalytic.tech/)

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: the dashboard is the easy half, the signals are what needs proving. GEX gets recomputed after the fact, so a backtest has to use the gamma reading as it stood that morning or it quietly knows the future. I'd publish a timestamped log of every AutoSignal first.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Building the backend with rate-limit balancing and caching is real engineering, and combining GEX with structure in one view is a reasonable idea. My honest opinion on what needs proof: GEX levels depend on assumptions (dealer positioning is estimated from open interest, not observed), so I'd show how the levels are calculated and how often price actually reacts to them compared with random levels, with the sample size. The AutoScanner needs a public record of every signal with its timestamp and outcome, tested against a simple trend-following baseline with costs. Since AI summaries are generated from data, linking each statement to the numbers behind it helps users check it. Backtest Labs at Cymetica is one place to see how strategies get tested against a benchmark.
